title: Under the Point
passages:
They went out through the gap where the door had swollen shut, Kornél first with the ledger against his chest, Ruzsa behind with the tarp over her head, Ákos last with Sára’s living hand knotted in his coat. The water was knee-deep and moving fast, pulling at their legs. The hut groaned behind them and settled. No one looked back.

Kornél stopped at the top of the sunken path. The ledger’s ink line ran from the page’s edge toward a drowned fence, then bent left, under the water. “Pilot’s mark,” he said. “The channel goes under the Point. We don’t cross the river. We go down it.” Ruzsa laughed once, without humor. “Under the Point is where the toll house keeps its dead.” Ákos held the notebook above the water. “Then that’s where Ilka’s name went.”

Sára’s dead hand rose from her side and pointed at the black water. Her living hand tightened on Ákos’s coat until he felt the seam give. He did not pull away. Kornél tied the cord to a post, tested it, and stepped down. The water took him to the waist. The cord went slack, then drew a short, hard line toward the left. He followed it. Ruzsa swore and followed. Ákos went after, Sára’s grip dragging at his coat, the ledger’s ink line bright under the rain.

At the bottom of the steps, the water was still. A stone shelf ran under the Point, dry except for a film of river. The ledger’s line ended at a crack in the stone. From the crack came a sound like a bell struck once, far off. Sára’s mouth shaped *Ilka*. The fourteenth mark on the page darkened, and a fifteenth began to form, thin as a hair.
